messages.text: checked the logs. it wasn't the context window. worker died on a null pointer in the vector normalize step. fixing now.
ok. while you patch that, i pulled the distribution of cosine similarities for the embedding stage across the 300 test strings.
zero hits above 0.92. max was 0.848. most cluster between 0.60 and 0.75. our auto-accept threshold is basically decorative right now.
that's... actually expected? nomic-embed-text isn't calibrated for this kind of conceptual distance. i saw the same thing when we tested it last week.
so adjudication is doing 100% of the heavy lifting. which means our latency is entirely dependent on qwen2.5-14b response time.
yeah. and if it's only seeing top-1 candidates because the similarity is low, it's guessing blind. we need to widen the candidate set.
i can add trigram near-misses as fallback candidates if embedding similarity < 0.85. that way the LLM has actual options to choose from, not just one weak match.
do it. also, let's drop the adjudication floor from 0.75 to 0.60. if we're sending borderline cases to the LLM anyway, might as well trust its judgment more.
wait, lower the floor? that means more strings go through adjudication. latency will spike.
only for the ones that were previously auto-rejected or borderline. and with trigram candidates added, the LLM should resolve them faster because it's not guessing from a single weak vector.
...ok, convinced. i'll push the trigram fallback and update the threshold config. re-running the 3 failed jobs now that your worker fix is in?
yes. and log which stage resolved each one this time. i want to see if trigram candidates actually improve adjudication accuracy.
